# vnrit 0.2.10 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/vnrit/0.2.10

# vnrit — Pure Rust X11 WebRTC Streaming Server

**vnrit** streams an X11 desktop to browsers over **WebRTC** with low-latency keyboard/mouse input forwarding. Built entirely in Rust — no GStreamer, no FFmpeg, no system codec dependencies.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        vnrit Server                              │
│                                                                  │
│  X11 Server ──→ SHM Capture ──→ libyuv I420 ──→ openh264 H.264  │
│  (Xvnc/Xvfb)     (MIT-SHM)        (SIMD ARM NEON)  (Screen RT)  │
│                                                                  │
│  PulseAudio ──→ Opus Encoder ───→ WebRTC                         │
│  (monitor src)     (libopus)       (webrtc-rs)                   │
│                                                                  │
│                        ↓                                         │
│  Browser ←──WebRTC─── WebSocket (signaling + input) → XTest      │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
## Features

- **Pure Rust**— zero GStreamer/FFmpeg dependency, ~6.6 MB release binary
- **WebRTC H.264**— openh264 encoder with screen content optimization
- **SIMD color conversion**— Google libyuv via ARM NEON
- **4-stage pipeline**— capture → convert → encode → send, fully parallel
- **Audio support**— PulseAudio → Opus (48kHz stereo, 20ms frames)
- **X11 input injection**— keyboard + mouse via XTest extension
- **MIT-SHM capture**— zero-copy shared memory screen capture
- **Browser cursor overlay**— CSS cursor synced separately, never encoded in video
- **Dual X11 connections**— separate sockets for capture and input (no lock contention)
- **Memory pool reuse**— zero per-frame allocations in steady state
- **Token authentication**— optional passwordless access control
- **Auto-reconnection**— exponential backoff (1s → 30s)
- **Touch-to-mouse**— tap, long-press, drag, scroll on touchscreens
- **Virtual keyboard**— on-screen keyboard for mobile/touch devices

## Quick Start

```
# Build
# Run (default: X11 :1, port 8080, 1000 kbps)
# Recommended settings for remote access
# Open http://<host>:8080 in a browser
```
## Prerequisites

| Dependency | Purpose | Install |
|---|---|---|
| Rust 1.82+ | Compiler | `rustup`or system package |
| cmake 3.20+ | libyuv build | `apt install cmake`/`pkg install cmake` |
| X11 server | Display to capture | Xvnc, Xvfb, or real X server |
| PulseAudio | Audio capture (optional) | `pulseaudio`server running |

### Termux (Android)

```
```
The X11 socket path at `/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/tmp/.X11-unix/X<display>` is auto-detected.

## Build

```
# Using build script
# Manual
CMAKE=
```
The `CMAKE` environment variable is required — `shiguredo_libyuv`'s build system
needs to find cmake on Android. Without it, the build.rs attempts to download
a prebuilt cmake binary, which fails on Termux.

### Git mirror for libyuv source

`shiguredo_libyuv` clones libyuv from `chromium.googlesource.com` during build.
If that's blocked on your network, configure a mirror:

```
```
## Usage

```
Usage: vnrit [OPTIONS]
Options:
      --display <DISPLAY>    X11 display to capture [default: :1]
  -p, --port <PORT>          HTTP/WebSocket listen port [default: 8080]
      --framerate <FPS>      Capture framerate [default: 24]
      --bitrate <KBPS>       Target bitrate in kbps [default: 1000]
      --height <PX>          Downscale height (0 = native) [default: 0]
      --stun <URL>           STUN server URL (empty to disable) [default: stun:stun.cloudflare.com:3478]
      --token <TOKEN>        Authentication token (optional)
      --log-level <LEVEL>    Log level: off, error, warn, info, debug, trace [default: warn]
  -h, --help                 Print help
```
### Examples

```
# Basic: stream :1 at native resolution
# Stream at 720p, 500 kbps (recommended for remote access)
# Higher quality for LAN
# Custom display and port
# With authentication
# Debug logging
# Disable STUN (LAN-only)
```
## Bitrate Guidelines (720p @ 24 fps)

| Bitrate | Quality | Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| 300 kbps | Low | Text terminals, SSH-like |
| 500 kbps | Good | GUI desktops (recommended) |
| 1000 kbps | High | Default, smooth desktop |
| 2000+ kbps | Near-lossless | Static content, reading |

## Architecture

### Video Pipeline

```
┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐
│ Capture  │───→│ Convert  │───→│ Encode   │───→│ Send     │
│ SHM/X11  │    │ libyuv   │    │ openh264 │    │ WebRTC   │
│ BGRA     │    │ I420     │    │ H.264    │    │ track    │
└──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘
  spawn_         spawn_          spawn_          async
  blocking       blocking        blocking
```
- **Capture**: X11 MIT-SHM extension reads screen pixels into shared memory (zero-copy). Falls back to- `get_image`if SHM unavailable.
- **Convert**: libyuv SIMD converts BGRA → I420. Supports I420-scaling for- `--height`downscale.
- **Encode**: openh264 H.264 encoder with- `ScreenContentRealTime`profile and configurable bitrate.
- **Send**: Asynchronously writes encoded frames to webrtc-rs- `TrackLocalStaticSample`.

All 4 stages run in parallel connected by bounded channels (capacity 4). Each stage holds its own pre-allocated buffer pool.

### Audio Pipeline

```
┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐
│ PulseAudio   │───→│ Opus     │───→│ WebRTC   │
│ Simple API   │    │ Encoder  │    │ track    │
│ PCM S16LE    │    │ 48kHz    │    │ 20ms     │
│ 3840 B/frame │    │ stereo   │    │ frames   │
└──────────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘
```
Audio is captured from the **default PulseAudio sink monitor** (system audio output). Falls back to default source (microphone) if monitor detection fails.

### Input Protocol

Commands are sent from the browser over the WebSocket as CSV:

| Command | Format | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Mouse move (relative) | `mr,dx,dy` | Relative cursor movement |
| Mouse move (absolute) | `ma,x,y` | Absolute cursor position |
| Mouse down | `md,button` | Button press (1=left, 2=middle, 3=right) |
| Mouse up | `mu,button` | Button release |
| Scroll | `ms,deltaY` | Scroll wheel |
| Key down | `kd,code` | `KeyboardEvent.code`(e.g.`KeyA`,`Digit2`) |
| Key up | `ku,code` | Key release |

Keycodes are physical (not character-based), so keyboard layout handling is done by the X server. Shift+2 produces `@` on a US layout, regardless of the browser's locale.

### WebSocket Signaling

```
Client → Server:  {"type":"ready"}
Server → Client:  {"type":"offer","sdp":"..."}
Client → Server:  {"type":"answer","sdp":"..."}
Both:             {"type":"ice","candidate":"...", "sdp_mline_index":0}
```
### Frontend

The built-in web UI (`src/index.html`) provides:

- **WebRTC video**via- `RTCPeerConnection`with H.264/Opus
- **CSS cursor overlay**— synced to server cursor position, never encoded in video
- **Relative input throttling**— accumulated via- `requestAnimationFrame`, not- `setInterval`
- **ResizeObserver**— real-time container resize tracking (no layout thrash)
- **Touch-to-mouse**: tap, long-press, drag, scroll
- **Virtual keyboard**: main/func/num layers with modifier latching
- **Auto-reconnection**with exponential backoff
- **Negotiation watchdog**: 15s timeout

### Cancellation & Cleanup

All pipeline tasks share a `CancellationToken`. On disconnect:

- `cancel.cancel()`signals all tasks
- Channel senders are dropped, waking blocked receivers
- Each task checks cancellation and exits cleanly
- `ice_forward`task exits naturally when its sender is dropped (no- `abort()`)
- All `spawn_blocking`handles are awaited

## Performance Optimizations

| Technique | Detail |
|---|---|
| Memory pool reuse | Pre-allocated Vecs per pipeline stage, no per-frame allocation |
| Zero-copy capture | MIT-SHM shared memory (no X11 socket transfer for pixels) |
| SIMD color conversion | libyuv ARGBToI420 + I420Scale via ARM NEON |
| Dual X11 connections | Separate sockets for capture and input (no mutex) |
| I420-domain scaling | Scale in YUV space (1.5 B/px vs 4 B/px for ARGB) |
| `with_resize_uninit` | Skip zero-initialization for buffers immediately overwritten |
| `SyncSender::send()` | Condition-variable-based blocking (no busy-wait) |
| `CancellationToken` | Unified cancellation for blocking + async tasks |
| Atomic memory ordering | `Release`/`Acquire`for ARM weak memory model |
| `Release`/`Acquire` | Correctness on ARM (phone) vs x86 |
| Repeat frame on error | If capture fails, repeat last frame (prevents decoder crash) |
| Force keyframe on error | If encode fails, reset encoder state immediately |
| `try_send`instead of`blocking_send` | No thread pool deadlock risk |

## Resource Usage

Measured on Snapdragon 835 (Adreno 540) at 720p 500 kbps:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Binary size | ~6.6 MB (release, stripped) |
| Memory (steady) | ~50-80 MB RSS |
| CPU (video, 24 fps) | 2-3 cores at ~1.5 GHz |
| CPU (audio, 20ms frames) | <5% of one core |
| Network bandwidth | ~500 kbps video + ~40 kbps audio |

## Troubleshooting

### Connection fails

- Check X11 server is running: `echo $DISPLAY`
- Confirm XTest extension: `xdpyinfo | grep XTest`
- Try direct connection: `vnrit --display :0 --stun ""`

### No audio

- Verify PulseAudio is running: `pactl info`
- Check default sink has a monitor: `pactl list sinks short`
- Set default source to monitor: `pactl set-default-source <sink>.monitor`

### Build errors

| Error | Fix |
|---|---|
| `cmake not found` | `apt install cmake`/`pkg install cmake` |
| `libclang not found` | `apt install libclang-dev`/`pkg install libclang` |
| `audiopus_sys build.rs` | Already patched in `vendor/`— no action needed |
| `chromium.googlesource.com timeout` | Configure git mirror (see Build section) |

# quorum-rs

Rust SDK **and** CLI for multi-agent deliberation systems — agents that propose, evaluate, and reach quorum on outcomes over a NATS-based orchestration protocol. Library and binary ship in the same crate.

## Install

As a library:

```
[]
 = "0.6"
```
As the `quorum` CLI (`run`, `status`, `trace`, `tui`, `init`):

```
```
Default features build the binary (`cli` + `tui`). To use as a pure library and skip the CLI deps (clap, ratatui, etc.):

```
[]
 = {  = "0.6",  = false,  = ["audit"] }
```
MSRV: Rust 1.85 (uses Edition 2024).

## CLI quick reference

```
quorum init                Bootstrap an `nsed.yaml` workspace config
quorum redeem <code>       Redeem a JWT invite — writes ~/.nsed/operator.token
                           and (for unified codes) ~/.nsed/agent.creds + .seed
quorum serve               Run an agent fleet from agent.yml. Reads creds
                           from ~/.nsed/agent.creds (default)
quorum run <task>          Submit a deliberation task to the orchestrator
quorum status              Health check + agent status
quorum trace <job_id>      Show a deliberation trace (verdict + evaluations)
quorum tui                 Interactive terminal UI (live deliberation view)
```
`run`, `status`, `trace`, `tui` read `./nsed.yaml` by default (`--config <path>` to override).
`serve` reads `./agent.yml` by default.

## What's inside

| Module | Key types | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `agents` | `NsedAgent`,`AgentContext`,`Proposal`,`Evaluation`,`ChatCapable`,`OutputLeakDetector` | Agent trait + deliberation data structures + pluggable output guard |
| `agents::config` | `AgentConfig`,`TaskPrecision` | Agent configuration (model, provider, limits) |
| `providers` | `ProviderFactory`,`ProviderRegistry`,`cli_base` | Dispatch registry mapping `provider.type`→ agent factory (register custom providers without forking);`cli_base`shares exec/mcp subprocess spawn + timeout helpers |
| `llms` | `AiModel`,`RequestConfig`,`SimpleOpenAIModel`,`OpenAICompatibleModel`,`RateLimiter` | LLM abstraction + production streaming client + simulator / stub for tests |
| `prompts` | `PromptSet`,`DefaultPromptSet` | Prompt template interface + benchmark-validated default proposer/evaluator templates |
| `tools` | `Tool`,`ToolDefinition`,`ScopedGrepTool`,`ScopedReadFileTool` | Tool-use interface (OpenAI function calling) + sandboxed filesystem tools |
| `workers` | `NatsNsedWorker`,`WorkerConfig`,`NatsScratchpadStore`,`WorkerHook`,`UserToolHandlerFactory` | NATS JetStream worker runtime |
| `middleware` | `AgentMiddleware`,`MiddlewarePipeline`,`MiddlewareConfig`,`RuleBasedMiddleware`,`LlmModerationMiddleware`,`BinaryMiddleware`,`DylibMiddleware` | Pluggable validation/moderation + YAML config + external-process dispatch |
| `status` | `AgentStatusSnapshot`,`SharedAgentStatus`,`server`,`multi_server` | Real-time status types + optional HTTP dashboard (feature `status-server`) |
| `nats_utils` | `connect_nats`,`sanitize_subject_component`,`NatsAuth` | NATS helpers + authentication |
| `telemetry` | `TelemetryEvent`,`TelemetryConfig`,`TelemetryEmitter` | Per-agent telemetry event catalog |

## Quick start — build a custom agent

```
use ;
use SimpleOpenAIModel;
use ;
use async_trait;
use Result;
async
```
## Use the reference agent

If you want the full ReAct loop, structured proposer/evaluator outputs, retry + repair, tool injection, and benchmark-validated prompts, use `ProposerEvaluatorAgent` instead of implementing `NsedAgent` from scratch:

```
use ;
use OpenAICompatibleModel;
use DefaultPromptSet;
use ;
# async
```
## Pre-built agent shells

For agents you don't write in Rust:

| Type | Use when |
|---|---|
| `ExecAgent` | The agent is a process you exec (any language); deliberation I/O via stdin/stdout JSON |
| `McpAgent`/`ClaudeAgent` | The agent is an MCP server (Claude Code, generic MCP) wrapped via the SDK runtime |

## Features

- `default = ["audit"]`
- `audit`— enables cryptographic signing of agent outputs via- `quorum-crypto-core`
- `status-server`— embedded axum dashboard for live agent + fleet status (HTTP)

# latuicon 0.1.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/latuicon/0.1.1

# 😴 latuicon

`latuicon`, the **lat**e **TUI** **icon** picker: a rip-off of the [late.sh](https://github.com/mpiorowski/late-sh) embedded icon picker.

A terminal UI icon picker for emoji, kaomoji, Unicode characters, and Nerd Font glyphs. Press Enter to print the selected icon to stdout; press Esc to exit without output.

## What's different from late.sh

The [initial commit](https://github.com/coko7/latuicon/commit/0fc806c) bootstrapped from the icon-picker component of [late.sh](https://github.com/mpiorowski/late-sh) (specifically code up until [6c670683](https://github.com/mpiorowski/late-sh/commit/6c670683e301cbef3df08683c84bc91141a0faee)). All development since then is independent.

Changes and additions:

- **Fuzzy search**🪄 — word-level Levenshtein matching so small typos still find the right icon (e.g.- `tumbs up`→ 👍)
- **Data files**📂 — emoji, kaomoji, unicode, and nerd font data extracted into editable JSON files under- `data/`
- **Centered layout**🎯 — subtitle under the title, icon-set block sized to content, search and icon list horizontally inset
- **Standalone binary**📦 — packaged as- `latuicon`, decoupled from the late.sh monorepo

Designed for shell capture:

```
icon=
```
## Install

```
```
### From source

```
```
Builds a release binary and installs it to `~/.local/bin/latuicon`.

## Usage

```
ICON_PICKER_THEME=dracula
```
Prints the chosen icon to stdout on confirm, nothing on Esc/Ctrl+C.

### Desktop integration example ([Hyprland](https://hypr.land/))

In my setup, I use [ floatty.sh](https://github.com/coko7/scripts/blob/main/global/floatty.sh) to open

`latuicon` in a floating terminal window and pipe the result to the clipboard. Here is my custom Hyprland binding for it:```
bindd = $mainMod, comma, laTUIcon icon picker, exec, FLOATTY_CAPTURE_OUTPUT=1 bash floatty.sh latuicon latuicon | wl-copy
```
And these are the Hyprland window rules for it:

```
# Special rules for floating/prompt terminals
windowrule {
    name = floater-kitty
    match:class = ^(floater-kitty-.*)$
    no_anim = on
    float = on
    center = on
    size = 1000 800
}
windowrule {
  name = floater-kitty-latuicon
  match:class = floater-kitty-latuicon
  size = 700 700
}
```
Pressing `$mainMod + ,` opens a floating terminal with the picker; confirming an icon copies it straight to the Wayland clipboard.

## Keybindings

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `↑`/`↓` | Navigate list |
| `Ctrl+K`/`Ctrl+J` | Navigate list (vi-style) |
| `PgUp`/`PgDn` | Page up / down |
| `Ctrl+U`/`Ctrl+D` | Half-page up / down |
| `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` | Switch tab |
| `Enter` | Select and exit |
| `Esc`/`Ctrl+C` | Exit without selecting |
| Type anything | Filter by name |
| `Ctrl+Z` | Undo search edit |
| Mouse click | Select tab or item |
| Double-click | Select and exit |
| Scroll wheel | Scroll list |

Search supports full emacs cursor movement (`Ctrl+A`, `Ctrl+E`, `Ctrl+F`, `Ctrl+B`, `Ctrl+W`, `Ctrl+Y`, etc.).

## Themes

`contrast` (default), `late`, `purple`, `mocha`, `gruvbox`, `dracula`

## Tabs

- **All**— every icon from every other tab, combined into one searchable set
- **Emoji**— common emoji + full emoji set
- **Kaomoji**— curated kaomoji collection
- **Unicode**— common symbols + Box Drawing, Geometric Shapes, Arrows, Math Operators, Dingbats; search supports- `U+XXXX`/- `0xXXXX`hex lookup and full Unicode name scan
- **Nerd Font**— common glyphs + full Nerd Font glyph set

# pdb-addr2line 0.12.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/pdb-addr2line/0.12.0

# pdb-addr2line

Resolve addresses to function names, and to file name and line number information, with the help of a PDB file. Inline stacks are supported.

The API of this crate is intended to be similar to the API of the
[ addr2line crate](https://docs.rs/addr2line/); the two

`Context` APIs
have comparable functionality. This crate is for PDB files whereas `addr2line`
is for DWARF data (which is used in ELF and mach-o binaries, for example).This crate also has a `TypeFormatter` API which can be used to get function signature
strings independently from a `Context`.

To create a `Context`, use `ContextPdbData`.

The implementation makes use of the excellent [ pdb crate](https://crates.io/crates/pdb).

## Example

```
use pdb; // (this is a re-export of the pdb crate)
```
# Command-line usage

This repository also contains a CLI executable modelled after addr2line.
You can install it using `cargo install`:

```
cargo install --examples pdb-addr2line
```
Here are some example uses:

```
$ curl -o dcomp.pdb -L "https://msdl.microsoft.com/download/symbols/dcomp.pdb/648B8DD0780A4E22FA7FA89B84633C231/dcomp.pdb"
$ pdb-addr2line --exe dcomp.pdb -fC 0x59aa0 0x52340 0x13498
Windows::UI::Composition::Compositor::Api::CreateScalarKeyFrameAnimation(Windows::UI::Composition::IScalarKeyFrameAnimation**)
??:?
std::map<unsigned int, Windows::UI::Composition::AnimationLoggingManager::ReferencedObject, std::less<unsigned int>, std::allocator<std::pair<unsigned int const, Windows::UI::Composition::AnimationLoggingManager::ReferencedObject> > >::_Try_emplace<unsigned int const&>(unsigned int const&)
??:?
DirectComposition::CDxDevice::RemoveGuardRect(ID3D11Texture2D*)
??:?
```
```
$ curl -o mozglue.pdb -L "https://github.com/mstange/profiler-get-symbols/raw/master/fixtures/win64-ci/mozglue.pdb"
$ pdb-addr2line -e mozglue.pdb -psfi 0x3b9fb
mozilla::JSONWriter::StartCollection(char const*, char const*, mozilla::JSONWriter::CollectionStyle) at JSONWriter.h:318
 (inlined by) mozilla::JSONWriter::StartArrayProperty(char const*, mozilla::JSONWriter::CollectionStyle) at JSONWriter.h:417
 (inlined by) mozilla::JSONWriter::StartArrayElement(mozilla::JSONWriter::CollectionStyle) at JSONWriter.h:422
 (inlined by) mozilla::baseprofiler::AutoArraySchemaWriter::AutoArraySchemaWriter(mozilla::baseprofiler::SpliceableJSONWriter&, mozilla::baseprofiler::UniqueJSONStrings&) at ProfileBufferEntry.cpp:141
 (inlined by) mozilla::baseprofiler::WriteSample(mozilla::baseprofiler::SpliceableJSONWriter&, mozilla::baseprofiler::UniqueJSONStrings&, mozilla::baseprofiler::ProfileSample const&) at ProfileBufferEntry.cpp:361
 (inlined by) mozilla::baseprofiler::ProfileBuffer::StreamSamplesToJSON::<unnamed-tag>::operator()(mozilla::ProfileChunkedBuffer::Reader*) const at ProfileBufferEntry.cpp:809
```
# Performance

`pdb-addr2line` optimizes for speed over memory by caching parsed information.
The debug information about inlines, files and line numbers is parsed lazily where possible.

# pdb_addr2line - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/pdb-addr2line/0.12.0/target-redirect/pdb_addr2line/

## Expand description

Resolve addresses to function names, and to file name and line number information, with the help of a PDB file. Inline stacks are supported.

The API of this crate is intended to be similar to the API of the
[ addr2line crate](https://docs.rs/addr2line/); the two

[APIs have comparable functionality. This crate is for PDB files whereas](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)

`Context``addr2line`
is for DWARF data (which is used in ELF and mach-o binaries, for example).This crate also has a [ TypeFormatter](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeFormatter.html) API which can be used to get function signature
strings independently from a

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)

`Context`To create a [ Context](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html), use

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextPdbData.html)

`ContextPdbData`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use pdb_addr2line::pdb; // (this is a re-export of the pdb crate)
fn look_up_addresses<'s, S: pdb::Source<'s> + Send + 's>(stream: S, addresses: &[u32]) -> std::result::Result<(), pdb_addr2line::Error> {
    let pdb = pdb::PDB::open(stream)?;
    let context_data = pdb_addr2line::ContextPdbData::try_from_pdb(pdb)?;
    let context = context_data.make_context()?;
    for address in addresses {
        if let Some(procedure_frames) = context.find_frames(*address)? {
            eprintln!("0x{:x} - {} frames:", address, procedure_frames.frames.len());
            for frame in procedure_frames.frames {
                let line_str = frame.line.map(|l| format!("{}", l));
                eprintln!(
                    "     {} at {}:{}",
                    frame.function.as_deref().unwrap_or("<unknown>"),
                    frame.file.as_deref().unwrap_or("??"),
                    line_str.as_deref().unwrap_or("??"),
                )
            }
        } else {
            eprintln!("{:x} - no frames found", address);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [maybe_owned](https://docs.rs/maybe-owned/0.3.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/maybe_owned/index.html);
- `pub use`- [pdb](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Context](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)
- The main API of this crate. Resolves addresses to function information.
- [Context](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextPdbData.html)- PdbData
- Allows to easily create a `Context``pdb::PDB`
- [Frame](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html)
- One frame of the inline stack at the looked-up address.
- [Function](https://docs.rs/struct.Function.html)
- Basic information about a function.
- [Function](https://docs.rs/struct.FunctionFrames.html)- Frames
- The result of an address lookup from `Context::find_frames`
- [Function](https://docs.rs/struct.FunctionIter.html)- Iter
- An iterator over all functions in a `Context`
- [Module](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleSectionContribution.html)- Section - Contribution
- The order of the fields matters for the lexicographical sort.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeFormatter.html)- Formatter
- Allows printing function signatures, for example for use in stack traces.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeFormatterFlags.html)- Formatter - Flags
- Flags for `TypeFormatter`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Module](https://docs.rs/trait.ModuleProvider.html)- Provider
- This trait is only needed for consumers who want to call Context::new_from_parts or TypeFormatter::new_from_parts manually, instead of using ContextPdbData. If you use ContextPdbData you do not need to worry about this trait. This trait allows Context and TypeFormatter to request parsing of module info on-demand. It also does some lifetime acrobatics so that Context can cache objects which have a lifetime dependency on the module info.

# pdb_addr2line - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pdb-addr2line/0.12.0/pdb_addr2line/index.html

## Expand description

Resolve addresses to function names, and to file name and line number information, with the help of a PDB file. Inline stacks are supported.

The API of this crate is intended to be similar to the API of the
[ addr2line crate](https://docs.rs/addr2line/); the two

[APIs have comparable functionality. This crate is for PDB files whereas](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)

`Context``addr2line`
is for DWARF data (which is used in ELF and mach-o binaries, for example).This crate also has a [ TypeFormatter](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeFormatter.html) API which can be used to get function signature
strings independently from a

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)

`Context`To create a [ Context](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html), use

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextPdbData.html)

`ContextPdbData`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use pdb_addr2line::pdb; // (this is a re-export of the pdb crate)
fn look_up_addresses<'s, S: pdb::Source<'s> + Send + 's>(stream: S, addresses: &[u32]) -> std::result::Result<(), pdb_addr2line::Error> {
    let pdb = pdb::PDB::open(stream)?;
    let context_data = pdb_addr2line::ContextPdbData::try_from_pdb(pdb)?;
    let context = context_data.make_context()?;
    for address in addresses {
        if let Some(procedure_frames) = context.find_frames(*address)? {
            eprintln!("0x{:x} - {} frames:", address, procedure_frames.frames.len());
            for frame in procedure_frames.frames {
                let line_str = frame.line.map(|l| format!("{}", l));
                eprintln!(
                    "     {} at {}:{}",
                    frame.function.as_deref().unwrap_or("<unknown>"),
                    frame.file.as_deref().unwrap_or("??"),
                    line_str.as_deref().unwrap_or("??"),
                )
            }
        } else {
            eprintln!("{:x} - no frames found", address);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [maybe_owned](https://docs.rs/maybe-owned/0.3.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/maybe_owned/index.html);
- `pub use`- [pdb](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Context](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)
- The main API of this crate. Resolves addresses to function information.
- [Context](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextPdbData.html)- PdbData
- Allows to easily create a `Context``pdb::PDB`
- [Frame](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html)
- One frame of the inline stack at the looked-up address.
- [Function](https://docs.rs/struct.Function.html)
- Basic information about a function.
- [Function](https://docs.rs/struct.FunctionFrames.html)- Frames
- The result of an address lookup from `Context::find_frames`
- [Function](https://docs.rs/struct.FunctionIter.html)- Iter
- An iterator over all functions in a `Context`
- [Module](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleSectionContribution.html)- Section - Contribution
- The order of the fields matters for the lexicographical sort.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeFormatter.html)- Formatter
- Allows printing function signatures, for example for use in stack traces.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeFormatterFlags.html)- Formatter - Flags
- Flags for `TypeFormatter`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Module](https://docs.rs/trait.ModuleProvider.html)- Provider
- This trait is only needed for consumers who want to call Context::new_from_parts or TypeFormatter::new_from_parts manually, instead of using ContextPdbData. If you use ContextPdbData you do not need to worry about this trait. This trait allows Context and TypeFormatter to request parsing of module info on-demand. It also does some lifetime acrobatics so that Context can cache objects which have a lifetime dependency on the module info.

[281](#281)impl<'a, 's> Context<'a, 's> {
[282](#282)    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
[289](#289)    pub fn new_from_parts(
[290](#290)        module_info_provider: &'a (dyn ModuleProvider<'s> + Sync),
[291](#291)        sections: &[ImageSectionHeader],
[292](#292)        address_map: &'a AddressMap<'s>,
[293](#293)        global_symbols: &'a SymbolTable<'s>,
[294](#294)        string_table: Option<&'a StringTable<'s>>,
[295](#295)        debug_info: &'a DebugInformation,
[296](#296)        type_formatter: MaybeOwned<'a, TypeFormatter<'a, 's>>,
[297](#297)    ) -> Result<Self> {
[298](#298)        let mut global_functions = Vec::new();
[299](#299)
[300](#300)        let mut symbol_iter = global_symbols.iter();
[302](#302)        while let Some(symbol) = symbol_iter.next()? {
[303](#303)            if let S_PUB32 | S_PUB32_ST = symbol.raw_kind() {
[304](#304)                if let Ok(SymbolData::Public(PublicSymbol { name, offset, .. })) = symbol.parse() {
[305](#305)                    if is_executable_section(offset.section, sections) {
[306](#306)                        global_functions.push(PublicSymbolFunctionOrPlaceholder {
[307](#307)                            start_offset: offset,
[308](#308)                            name: Some(name),
[309](#309)                        });
[310](#310)                    }
[311](#311)                }
[312](#312)            }
[313](#313)        }
[314](#314)
[315](#315)        let section_contributions =
[323](#323)            compute_section_contributions(debug_info, sections, &mut global_functions)?;
[324](#324)
[325](#325)        for (section_index_zero_based, section) in sections.iter().enumerate() {
[328](#328)            let section_index = (section_index_zero_based + 1) as u16;
[329](#329)            if !is_executable_section(section_index, sections) {
[330](#330)                continue;
[331](#331)            }
[332](#332)            let size = section.virtual_size;
[333](#333)            let section_end_offset = PdbInternalSectionOffset::new(section_index, size);
[334](#334)            global_functions.push(PublicSymbolFunctionOrPlaceholder {
[335](#335)                start_offset: section_end_offset,
[336](#336)                name: None,
[337](#337)            });
[338](#338)        }
[339](#339)
[340](#340)        global_functions.sort_by_key(|p| {
[347](#347)            (
[348](#348)                p.start_offset.section,
[349](#349)                p.start_offset.offset,
[350](#350)                p.name.is_none(),
[351](#351)            )
[352](#352)        });
[353](#353)        global_functions.dedup_by_key(|p| p.start_offset);
[354](#354)
[355](#355)        Ok(Self {
[356](#356)            address_map,
[357](#357)            section_contributions,
[358](#358)            string_table,
[359](#359)            type_formatter,
[360](#360)            global_functions,
[361](#361)            cache: RefCell::new(ContextCache {
[362](#362)                module_cache: BasicModuleInfoCache {
[363](#363)                    cache: Default::default(),
[364](#364)                    module_info_provider,
[365](#365)                },
[366](#366)                function_line_cache: Default::default(),
[367](#367)                procedure_cache: Default::default(),
[368](#368)                extended_module_cache: Default::default(),
[369](#369)                inline_name_cache: Default::default(),
[370](#370)                full_rva_list: Default::default(),
[371](#371)            }),
[372](#372)        })
[373](#373)    }

[398](#398)    pub fn find_function(&self, probe: u32) -> Result<Option<Function>> {
[402](#402)        let offset = match Rva(probe).to_internal_offset(self.address_map) {
[403](#403)            Some(offset) => offset,
[404](#404)            None => return Ok(None),
[405](#405)        };
[406](#406)
[407](#407)        let mut cache = self.cache.borrow_mut();
[408](#408)        let ContextCache {
[409](#409)            module_cache,
[410](#410)            procedure_cache,
[411](#411)            ..
[412](#412)        } = &mut *cache;
[413](#413)
[414](#414)        let func = match self.lookup_function(offset, module_cache) {
[415](#415)            Some(func) => func,
[416](#416)            None => return Ok(None),
[417](#417)        };
[418](#418)
[419](#419)        match func {
[420](#420)            PublicOrProcedureSymbol::Public(_, _, global_function_index) => {
[421](#421)                let func = &self.global_functions[global_function_index];
[422](#422)                let name = func.name.map(|name| name.to_string().to_string());
[423](#423)                let start_rva = match func.start_offset.to_rva(self.address_map) {
[424](#424)                    Some(rva) => rva.0,
[425](#425)                    None => return Ok(None),
[426](#426)                };
[427](#427)                let end_rva = match self.global_functions.get(global_function_index + 1) {
[429](#429)                    Some(next_entry)
[430](#430)                        if next_entry.start_offset.section == func.start_offset.section =>
[431](#431)                    {
[432](#432)                        match next_entry.start_offset.to_rva(self.address_map) {
[433](#433)                            Some(rva) => Some(rva.0),
[434](#434)                            None => return Ok(None),
[435](#435)                        }
[436](#436)                    }
[437](#437)                    _ => None,
[438](#438)                };
[439](#439)                Ok(Some(Function {
[440](#440)                    start_rva,
[441](#441)                    end_rva,
[442](#442)                    name,
[443](#443)                }))
[444](#444)            }
[445](#445)            PublicOrProcedureSymbol::Procedure(module_index, _, func) => {
[446](#446)                let extended_info = procedure_cache.entry(func.offset).or_default();
[447](#447)                let name = extended_info
[448](#448)                    .get_name(
[449](#449)                        func,
[450](#450)                        &self.type_formatter,
[451](#451)                        &self.global_functions,
[452](#452)                        module_index,
[453](#453)                    )
[454](#454)                    .map(String::from);
[455](#455)                let start_rva = match func.offset.to_rva(self.address_map) {
[456](#456)                    Some(rva) => rva.0,
[457](#457)                    None => return Ok(None),
[458](#458)                };
[459](#459)                let end_rva = start_rva + func.len;
[460](#460)                Ok(Some(Function {
[461](#461)                    start_rva,
[462](#462)                    end_rva: Some(end_rva),
[463](#463)                    name,
[464](#464)                }))
[465](#465)            }
[466](#466)        }
[467](#467)    }

[469](#469)    pub fn find_frames(&self, probe: u32) -> Result<Option<FunctionFrames<'_>>> {
[476](#476)        let offset = match Rva(probe).to_internal_offset(self.address_map) {
[477](#477)            Some(offset) => offset,
[478](#478)            None => return Ok(None),
[479](#479)        };
[480](#480)
[481](#481)        let mut cache = self.cache.borrow_mut();
[482](#482)        let ContextCache {
[483](#483)            module_cache,
[484](#484)            procedure_cache,
[485](#485)            function_line_cache,
[486](#486)            extended_module_cache,
[487](#487)            inline_name_cache,
[488](#488)            ..
[489](#489)        } = &mut *cache;
[490](#490)
[491](#491)        let func = match self.lookup_function(offset, module_cache) {
[492](#492)            Some(func) => func,
[493](#493)            None => return Ok(None),
[494](#494)        };
[495](#495)
[496](#496)        let (module_index, module_info, func_offset, func_size, func_name, proc_stuff) = match func
[504](#504)        {
[505](#505)            PublicOrProcedureSymbol::Public(module_index, module_info, global_function_index) => {
[506](#506)                let func = &self.global_functions[global_function_index];
[507](#507)                let func_name = func.name.map(|name| name.to_string().to_string());
[508](#508)                let size = match self.global_functions.get(global_function_index + 1) {
[510](#510)                    Some(next_entry)
[511](#511)                        if next_entry.start_offset.section == func.start_offset.section =>
[512](#512)                    {
[513](#513)                        Some(next_entry.start_offset.offset - func.start_offset.offset)
[514](#514)                    }
[515](#515)                    _ => None,
[516](#516)                };
[517](#517)                (
[518](#518)                    module_index,
[519](#519)                    module_info,
[520](#520)                    func.start_offset,
[521](#521)                    size,
[522](#522)                    func_name,
[523](#523)                    None,
[524](#524)                )
[525](#525)            }
[526](#526)            PublicOrProcedureSymbol::Procedure(module_index, module_info, proc) => {
[527](#527)                let proc_extended_info = procedure_cache.entry(proc.offset).or_default();
[528](#528)                let func_name = proc_extended_info
[529](#529)                    .get_name(
[530](#530)                        proc,
[531](#531)                        &self.type_formatter,
[532](#532)                        &self.global_functions,
[533](#533)                        module_index,
[534](#534)                    )
[535](#535)                    .map(String::from);
[536](#536)                (
[537](#537)                    module_index,
[538](#538)                    Some(module_info),
[539](#539)                    proc.offset,
[540](#540)                    Some(proc.len),
[541](#541)                    func_name,
[542](#542)                    Some((proc, proc_extended_info)),
[543](#543)                )
[544](#544)            }
[545](#545)        };
[546](#546)
[547](#547)        let extended_module_info = match module_info {
[548](#548)            Some(module_info) => Some(
[549](#549)                extended_module_cache
[550](#550)                    .entry(module_index)
[551](#551)                    .or_insert_with(|| self.compute_extended_module_info(module_info))
[552](#552)                    .as_mut()
[553](#553)                    .map_err(|err| mem::replace(err, Error::ExtendedModuleInfoUnsuccessful))?,
[554](#554)            ),
[555](#555)            None => None,
[556](#556)        };
[557](#557)
[558](#558)        let (file, line) = if let Some(ExtendedModuleInfo { line_program, .. }) =
[559](#559)            &extended_module_info
[560](#560)        {
[561](#561)            let function_line_info = function_line_cache.entry(func_offset).or_default();
[562](#562)            let lines = function_line_info.get_lines(func_offset, line_program)?;
[563](#563)            let search = match lines.binary_search_by_key(&offset.offset, |li| li.start_offset) {
[564](#564)                Err(0) => None,
[565](#565)                Ok(i) => Some(i),
[566](#566)                Err(i) => Some(i - 1),
[567](#567)            };
[568](#568)            match search {
[569](#569)                Some(index) => {
[570](#570)                    let line_info = &lines[index];
[571](#571)                    (
[572](#572)                        self.resolve_filename(line_program, line_info.file_index),
[573](#573)                        Some(line_info.line_start),
[574](#574)                    )
[575](#575)                }
[576](#576)                None => (None, None),
[577](#577)            }
[578](#578)        } else {
[579](#579)            (None, None)
[580](#580)        };
[581](#581)
[582](#582)        let frame = Frame {
[583](#583)            function: func_name,
[584](#584)            file,
[585](#585)            line,
[586](#586)        };
[587](#587)
[588](#588)        let mut frames = vec![frame];
[590](#590)
[591](#591)        if let (Some((proc, proc_extended_info)), Some(extended_module_info)) =
[592](#592)            (proc_stuff, extended_module_info)
[593](#593)        {
[594](#594)            let ExtendedModuleInfo {
[595](#595)                inlinees,
[596](#596)                line_program,
[597](#597)                module_info,
[598](#598)                ..
[599](#599)            } = extended_module_info;
[600](#600)            let mut inline_ranges =
[601](#601)                proc_extended_info.get_inline_ranges(module_info, proc, inlinees)?;
[602](#602)
[603](#603)            loop {
[604](#604)                let current_depth = (frames.len() - 1) as u16;
[605](#605)
[606](#606)                let search = inline_ranges.binary_search_by(|range| {
[611](#611)                    if range.call_depth > current_depth {
[612](#612)                        Ordering::Greater
[613](#613)                    } else if range.call_depth < current_depth {
[614](#614)                        Ordering::Less
[615](#615)                    } else if range.start_offset > offset.offset {
[616](#616)                        Ordering::Greater
[617](#617)                    } else if range.end_offset <= offset.offset {
[618](#618)                        Ordering::Less
[619](#619)                    } else {
[620](#620)                        Ordering::Equal
[621](#621)                    }
[622](#622)                });
[623](#623)                let (inline_range, remainder) = match search {
[624](#624)                    Ok(index) => (&inline_ranges[index], &inline_ranges[index + 1..]),
[625](#625)                    Err(_) => break,
[626](#626)                };
[627](#627)
[628](#628)                let function = inline_name_cache
[629](#629)                    .entry(inline_range.inlinee)
[630](#630)                    .or_insert_with(|| {
[631](#631)                        self.type_formatter
[632](#632)                            .format_id(module_index, inline_range.inlinee)
[633](#633)                    })
[634](#634)                    .as_ref()
[635](#635)                    .ok()
[636](#636)                    .cloned();
[637](#637)                let file = inline_range
[638](#638)                    .file_index
[639](#639)                    .and_then(|file_index| self.resolve_filename(line_program, file_index));
[640](#640)                let line = inline_range.line_start;
[641](#641)                frames.push(Frame {
[642](#642)                    function,
[643](#643)                    file,
[644](#644)                    line,
[645](#645)                });
[646](#646)
[647](#647)                inline_ranges = remainder;
[648](#648)            }
[649](#649)
[650](#650)            frames.reverse();
[652](#652)        }
[653](#653)
[654](#654)        let start_rva = match func_offset.to_rva(self.address_map) {
[655](#655)            Some(rva) => rva.0,
[656](#656)            None => return Ok(None),
[657](#657)        };
[658](#658)        let end_rva = func_size.and_then(|size| start_rva.checked_add(size));
[659](#659)
[660](#660)        Ok(Some(FunctionFrames {
[661](#661)            start_rva,
[662](#662)            end_rva,
[663](#663)            frames,
[664](#664)        }))
[665](#665)    }
[666](#666)
[667](#667)    fn compute_full_rva_list(&self, module_cache: &mut BasicModuleInfoCache<'a, 's>) -> Vec<u32> {
[668](#668)        let mut list = Vec::new();
[669](#669)        for func in &self.global_functions {
[670](#670)            if let Some(rva) = func.start_offset.to_rva(self.address_map) {
[671](#671)                list.push(rva.0);
[672](#672)            }
[673](#673)        }
[674](#674)        for module_index in 0..self.type_formatter.modules().len() {
[675](#675)            if let Some(BasicModuleInfo { procedures, .. }) =
[676](#676)                module_cache.get_basic_module_info(self.type_formatter.modules(), module_index)
[677](#677)            {
[678](#678)                for proc in procedures {
[679](#679)                    if let Some(rva) = proc.offset.to_rva(self.address_map) {
[680](#680)                        list.push(rva.0);
[681](#681)                    }
[682](#682)                }
[683](#683)            }
[684](#684)        }
[685](#685)        list.sort_unstable();
[686](#686)        list.dedup();
[687](#687)        list
[688](#688)    }
[689](#689)
[690](#690)    fn lookup_function<'m>(
[691](#691)        &self,
[692](#692)        offset: PdbInternalSectionOffset,
[693](#693)        module_cache: &'m mut BasicModuleInfoCache<'a, 's>,
[694](#694)    ) -> Option<PublicOrProcedureSymbol<'a, 's, 'm>> {
[695](#695)        let sc_index = match self.section_contributions.binary_search_by(|sc| {
[696](#696)            if sc.section_index < offset.section {
[697](#697)                Ordering::Less
[698](#698)            } else if sc.section_index > offset.section {
[699](#699)                Ordering::Greater
[700](#700)            } else if sc.end_offset <= offset.offset {
[701](#701)                Ordering::Less
[702](#702)            } else if sc.start_offset > offset.offset {
[703](#703)                Ordering::Greater
[704](#704)            } else {
[705](#705)                Ordering::Equal
[706](#706)            }
[707](#707)        }) {
[708](#708)            Ok(sc_index) => sc_index,
[709](#709)            Err(_) => {
[710](#710)                return None;
[712](#712)            }
[713](#713)        };
[714](#714)
[715](#715)        let sc = &self.section_contributions[sc_index];
[716](#716)        let basic_module_info =
[717](#717)            module_cache.get_basic_module_info(self.type_formatter.modules(), sc.module_index);
[718](#718)
[719](#719)        let module_info = if let Some(BasicModuleInfo {
[720](#720)            procedures,
[721](#721)            module_info,
[722](#722)        }) = basic_module_info
[723](#723)        {
[724](#724)            if let Ok(procedure_index) = procedures.binary_search_by(|p| {
[725](#725)                if p.offset.section < offset.section {
[726](#726)                    Ordering::Less
[727](#727)                } else if p.offset.section > offset.section {
[728](#728)                    Ordering::Greater
[729](#729)                } else if p.offset.offset + p.len <= offset.offset {
[730](#730)                    Ordering::Less
[731](#731)                } else if p.offset.offset > offset.offset {
[732](#732)                    Ordering::Greater
[733](#733)                } else {
[734](#734)                    Ordering::Equal
[735](#735)                }
[736](#736)            }) {
[737](#737)                return Some(PublicOrProcedureSymbol::Procedure(
[739](#739)                    sc.module_index,
[740](#740)                    module_info,
[741](#741)                    &procedures[procedure_index],
[742](#742)                ));
[743](#743)            }
[744](#744)            Some(*module_info)
[745](#745)        } else {
[746](#746)            None
[747](#747)        };
[748](#748)
[749](#749)        let last_global_function_starting_lte_address = match self
[755](#755)            .global_functions
[756](#756)            .binary_search_by_key(&(offset.section, offset.offset), |p| {
[757](#757)                (p.start_offset.section, p.start_offset.offset)
[758](#758)            }) {
[759](#759)            Err(0) => return None,
[760](#760)            Ok(i) => i,
[761](#761)            Err(i) => i - 1,
[762](#762)        };
[763](#763)        let fun = &self.global_functions[last_global_function_starting_lte_address];
[764](#764)        debug_assert!(
[765](#765)            fun.start_offset.section < offset.section
[766](#766)                || (fun.start_offset.section == offset.section
[767](#767)                    && fun.start_offset.offset <= offset.offset)
[768](#768)        );
[769](#769)        if fun.start_offset.section != offset.section {
[770](#770)            return None;
[771](#771)        }
[772](#772)        if fun.start_offset.offset < sc.start_offset {
[774](#774)            return None;
[775](#775)        }
[776](#776)
[777](#777)        Some(PublicOrProcedureSymbol::Public(
[778](#778)            sc.module_index,
[779](#779)            module_info,
[780](#780)            last_global_function_starting_lte_address,
[781](#781)        ))
[782](#782)    }
[783](#783)
[784](#784)    fn compute_extended_module_info(
[785](#785)        &self,
[786](#786)        module_info: &'a ModuleInfo<'s>,
[787](#787)    ) -> Result<ExtendedModuleInfo<'a, 's>> {
[788](#788)        let line_program = module_info.line_program()?;
[789](#789)
[790](#790)        let inlinees: BTreeMap<IdIndex, Inlinee> = module_info
[791](#791)            .inlinees()?
[792](#792)            .map(|i| Ok((i.index(), i)))
[793](#793)            .collect()?;
[794](#794)
[795](#795)        Ok(ExtendedModuleInfo {
[796](#796)            module_info,
[797](#797)            inlinees,
[798](#798)            line_program,
[799](#799)        })
[800](#800)    }
[801](#801)
[802](#802)    fn resolve_filename(
[803](#803)        &self,
[804](#804)        line_program: &LineProgram,
[805](#805)        file_index: FileIndex,
[806](#806)    ) -> Option<Cow<'a, str>> {
[807](#807)        if let Some(string_table) = self.string_table {
[808](#808)            if let Ok(file_info) = line_program.get_file_info(file_index) {
[809](#809)                return file_info.name.to_string_lossy(string_table).ok();
[810](#810)            }
[811](#811)        }
[812](#812)        None
[813](#813)    }
[814](#814)}

[816](#816)#[derive(Clone)]
[818](#818)pub struct FunctionIter<'c, 'a, 's> {
[819](#819)    context: &'c Context<'a, 's>,
[820](#820)    full_rva_list: Arc<Vec<u32>>,
[821](#821)    cur_index: usize,
[822](#822)}
[823](#823)
[824](#824)impl Iterator for FunctionIter<'_, '_, '_> {
[825](#825)    type Item = Function;
[826](#826)
[827](#827)    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Function> {
[828](#828)        loop {
[829](#829)            if self.cur_index >= self.full_rva_list.len() {
[830](#830)                return None;
[831](#831)            }
[832](#832)            let rva = self.full_rva_list[self.cur_index];
[833](#833)            self.cur_index += 1;
[834](#834)            if let Ok(Some(fun)) = self.context.find_function(rva) {
[835](#835)                return Some(fun);
[836](#836)            }
[837](#837)        }
[838](#838)    }

[850](#850)struct BasicModuleInfoCache<'a, 's> {
[851](#851)    cache: HashMap<usize, Option<BasicModuleInfo<'a, 's>>>,
[852](#852)    module_info_provider: &'a (dyn ModuleProvider<'s> + Sync),
[853](#853)}
[854](#854)
[855](#855)impl<'a, 's> BasicModuleInfoCache<'a, 's> {
[856](#856)    pub fn get_basic_module_info(
[857](#857)        &mut self,
[858](#858)        modules: &[Module<'a>],
[859](#859)        module_index: usize,
[860](#860)    ) -> Option<&BasicModuleInfo<'a, 's>> {
[861](#861)        let module_info_provider = self.module_info_provider;
[863](#863)
[864](#864)        self.cache
[865](#865)            .entry(module_index)
[866](#866)            .or_insert_with(|| {
[867](#867)                let module = modules.get(module_index)?;
[868](#868)                let module_info = module_info_provider
[869](#869)                    .get_module_info(module_index, module)
[870](#870)                    .ok()??;
[871](#871)                BasicModuleInfo::try_from_module_info(module_info).ok()
[872](#872)            })
[873](#873)            .as_ref()
[874](#874)    }
[875](#875)}
[876](#876)
[877](#877)struct BasicModuleInfo<'a, 's> {
[878](#878)    module_info: &'a ModuleInfo<'s>,
[879](#879)    procedures: Vec<ProcedureSymbolFunction<'a>>,
[880](#880)}
[881](#881)
[882](#882)impl<'a, 's> BasicModuleInfo<'a, 's> {
[883](#883)    pub fn try_from_module_info(
[884](#884)        module_info: &'a ModuleInfo<'s>,
[885](#885)    ) -> Result<BasicModuleInfo<'a, 's>> {
[886](#886)        let mut symbols_iter = module_info.symbols()?;
[887](#887)        let mut functions = Vec::new();
[888](#888)        while let Some(symbol) = symbols_iter.next()? {
[889](#889)            if let S_LPROC32 | S_LPROC32_ST | S_GPROC32 | S_GPROC32_ST | S_LPROC32_ID
[890](#890)            | S_GPROC32_ID | S_LPROC32_DPC | S_LPROC32_DPC_ID | S_THUNK32 | S_THUNK32_ST
[891](#891)            | S_SEPCODE = symbol.raw_kind()
[892](#892)            {
[893](#893)                match symbol.parse() {
[894](#894)                    Ok(SymbolData::Procedure(proc)) => {
[895](#895)                        if proc.len == 0 {
[896](#896)                            continue;
[897](#897)                        }
[898](#898)
[899](#899)                        functions.push(ProcedureSymbolFunction {
[900](#900)                            offset: proc.offset,
[901](#901)                            len: proc.len,
[902](#902)                            name: proc.name,
[903](#903)                            symbol_index: symbol.index(),
[904](#904)                            end_symbol_index: proc.end,
[905](#905)                            type_index: proc.type_index,
[906](#906)                        });
[907](#907)                    }
[908](#908)                    Ok(SymbolData::SeparatedCode(data)) => {
[909](#909)                        if data.len == 0 {
[910](#910)                            continue;
[911](#911)                        }
[912](#912)
[913](#913)                        let (name, type_index) = match functions.last() {
[917](#917)                            Some(proc) if proc.offset == data.parent_offset => {
[918](#918)                                (proc.name, proc.type_index)
[919](#919)                            }
[920](#920)                            _ => continue,
[921](#921)                        };
[922](#922)
[923](#923)                        functions.push(ProcedureSymbolFunction {
[924](#924)                            offset: data.offset,
[925](#925)                            len: data.len,
[926](#926)                            name,
[927](#927)                            symbol_index: symbol.index(),
[928](#928)                            end_symbol_index: data.end,
[929](#929)                            type_index,
[930](#930)                        });
[931](#931)                    }
[932](#932)                    Ok(SymbolData::Thunk(thunk)) => {
[933](#933)                        if thunk.len == 0 {
[934](#934)                            continue;
[935](#935)                        }
[936](#936)
[937](#937)                        functions.push(ProcedureSymbolFunction {
[940](#940)                            offset: thunk.offset,
[941](#941)                            len: thunk.len as u32,
[942](#942)                            name: thunk.name,
[943](#943)                            symbol_index: symbol.index(),
[944](#944)                            end_symbol_index: thunk.end,
[945](#945)                            type_index: TypeIndex(0),
[946](#946)                        });
[947](#947)                    }
[948](#948)                    _ => {}
[949](#949)                }
[950](#950)            }
[951](#951)        }
[952](#952)        functions.sort_by_key(|p| (p.offset.section, p.offset.offset));
[956](#956)        functions.dedup_by_key(|p| p.offset);
[957](#957)
[958](#958)        Ok(BasicModuleInfo {
[959](#959)            module_info,
[960](#960)            procedures: functions,
[961](#961)        })
[962](#962)    }
[963](#963)}
[964](#964)
[965](#965)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialOrd, PartialEq, Eq, Ord)]
[967](#967)pub struct ModuleSectionContribution {
[968](#968)    section_index: u16,
[969](#969)    start_offset: u32,
[970](#970)    end_offset: u32,
[971](#971)    module_index: usize,
[972](#972)}
[973](#973)
[974](#974)fn compute_section_contributions(
[980](#980)    debug_info: &DebugInformation<'_>,
[981](#981)    sections: &[ImageSectionHeader],
[982](#982)    placeholder_functions: &mut Vec<PublicSymbolFunctionOrPlaceholder>,
[983](#983)) -> Result<Vec<ModuleSectionContribution>> {
[984](#984)    let mut section_contribution_iter = debug_info
[985](#985)        .section_contributions()?
[986](#986)        .filter(|sc| Ok(sc.size != 0 && is_executable_section(sc.offset.section, sections)));
[987](#987)    let mut section_contributions = Vec::new();
[988](#988)
[989](#989)    if let Some(first_sc) = section_contribution_iter.next()? {
[990](#990)        let mut current_combined_sc = ModuleSectionContribution {
[991](#991)            section_index: first_sc.offset.section,
[992](#992)            start_offset: first_sc.offset.offset,
[993](#993)            end_offset: first_sc.offset.offset + first_sc.size,
[994](#994)            module_index: first_sc.module,
[995](#995)        };
[996](#996)        let mut is_executable = is_executable_section(first_sc.offset.section, sections);
[997](#997)
[998](#998)        while let Some(sc) = section_contribution_iter.next()? {
[1001](#1001)            let section_index = sc.offset.section;
[1002](#1002)            let start_offset = sc.offset.offset;
[1003](#1003)            let end_offset = start_offset + sc.size;
[1004](#1004)            let module_index = sc.module;
[1005](#1005)            if section_index == current_combined_sc.section_index
[1006](#1006)                && module_index == current_combined_sc.module_index
[1007](#1007)            {
[1008](#1008)                if end_offset < current_combined_sc.end_offset {
[1011](#1011)                    return Err(Error::UnorderedSectionContributions(
[1012](#1012)                        module_index,
[1013](#1013)                        section_index,
[1014](#1014)                    ));
[1015](#1015)                }
[1016](#1016)
[1017](#1017)                current_combined_sc.end_offset = end_offset;
[1019](#1019)            } else {
[1020](#1020)                section_contributions.push(current_combined_sc);
[1021](#1021)                current_combined_sc = ModuleSectionContribution {
[1022](#1022)                    section_index: sc.offset.section,
[1023](#1023)                    start_offset: sc.offset.offset,
[1024](#1024)                    end_offset,
[1025](#1025)                    module_index: sc.module,
[1026](#1026)                };
[1027](#1027)                is_executable = is_executable_section(sc.offset.section, sections);
[1028](#1028)            }
[1029](#1029)
[1030](#1030)            if is_executable {
[1031](#1031)                placeholder_functions.push(PublicSymbolFunctionOrPlaceholder {
[1032](#1032)                    start_offset: sc.offset,
[1033](#1033)                    name: None,
[1034](#1034)                });
[1035](#1035)            }
[1036](#1036)        }
[1037](#1037)        section_contributions.push(current_combined_sc);
[1038](#1038)    }
[1039](#1039)
[1040](#1040)    section_contributions.sort_unstable();
[1042](#1042)
[1043](#1043)    if let Some((first_sc, rest)) = section_contributions.split_first() {
[1045](#1045)        let mut prev_sc = first_sc;
[1046](#1046)        for sc in rest {
[1047](#1047)            if sc.section_index == prev_sc.section_index && sc.start_offset < prev_sc.end_offset {
[1048](#1048)                return Err(Error::OverlappingSectionContributions(
[1049](#1049)                    sc.section_index,
[1050](#1050)                    prev_sc.module_index,
[1051](#1051)                    sc.module_index,
[1052](#1052)                ));
[1053](#1053)            }
[1054](#1054)            prev_sc = sc;
[1055](#1055)        }
[1056](#1056)    }
[1057](#1057)
[1058](#1058)    Ok(section_contributions)
[1059](#1059)}
[1060](#1060)
[1061](#1061)fn get_section(section_index: u16, sections: &[ImageSectionHeader]) -> Option<&ImageSectionHeader> {
[1063](#1063)    if section_index == 0 {
[1064](#1064)        None
[1065](#1065)    } else {
[1066](#1066)        sections.get((section_index - 1) as usize)
[1067](#1067)    }
[1068](#1068)}
[1069](#1069)
[1070](#1070)fn is_executable_section(section_index: u16, sections: &[ImageSectionHeader]) -> bool {
[1072](#1072)    match get_section(section_index, sections) {
[1073](#1073)        Some(section) => section.characteristics.execute(), None => false,
[1075](#1075)    }
[1076](#1076)}
[1077](#1077)
[1078](#1078)#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
[1081](#1081)struct PublicSymbolFunctionOrPlaceholder<'s> {
[1082](#1082)    start_offset: PdbInternalSectionOffset,
[1087](#1087)    name: Option<RawString<'s>>,
[1090](#1090)}
[1091](#1091)
[1092](#1092)#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
[1093](#1093)struct ProcedureSymbolFunction<'a> {
[1094](#1094)    offset: PdbInternalSectionOffset,
[1096](#1096)    len: u32,

[1160](#1160)    fn get_name(
[1161](#1161)        &mut self,
[1162](#1162)        proc: &ProcedureSymbolFunction,

[1164](#1164)        global_functions: &[PublicSymbolFunctionOrPlaceholder],
[1165](#1165)        module_index: usize,

[1170](#1170)                    if let Ok(public_fun_index) = global_functions
[1175](#1175)                        .binary_search_by_key(&(proc.offset.section, proc.offset.offset), |f| {
[1176](#1176)                            (f.start_offset.section, f.start_offset.offset)

[1188](#1188)                    .ok()

[1193](#1193)    fn get_inline_ranges(

[1202](#1202)            .as_mut()

[1206](#1206)}
[1207](#1207)
[1208](#1208)fn compute_procedure_inline_ranges(
[1209](#1209)    module_info: &ModuleInfo,
[1210](#1210)    proc: &ProcedureSymbolFunction,
[1211](#1211)    inlinees: &BTreeMap<IdIndex, Inlinee>,
[1212](#1212)) -> Result<Vec<InlineRange>> {
[1213](#1213)    let mut lines = Vec::new();
[1214](#1214)    let mut symbols_iter = module_info.symbols_at(proc.symbol_index)?;
[1215](#1215)    let _proc_sym = symbols_iter.next()?;
[1216](#1216)    while let Some(symbol) = symbols_iter.next()? {
[1217](#1217)        if symbol.index() >= proc.end_symbol_index {
[1218](#1218)            break;
[1219](#1219)        }
[1220](#1220)        if let S_LPROC32 | S_LPROC32_ST | S_GPROC32 | S_GPROC32_ST | S_LPROC32_ID | S_GPROC32_ID
[1221](#1221)        | S_LPROC32_DPC | S_LPROC32_DPC_ID | S_INLINESITE | S_INLINESITE2 = symbol.raw_kind()
[1222](#1222)        {
[1223](#1223)            match symbol.parse() {
[1224](#1224)                Ok(SymbolData::Procedure(p)) => {
[1225](#1225)                    symbols_iter.skip_to(p.end)?;
[1227](#1227)                }
[1228](#1228)                Ok(SymbolData::InlineSite(site)) => {
[1229](#1229)                    process_inlinee_symbols(
[1230](#1230)                        &mut symbols_iter,
[1231](#1231)                        inlinees,
[1232](#1232)                        proc.offset,
[1233](#1233)                        site,
[1234](#1234)                        0,
[1235](#1235)                        &mut lines,
[1236](#1236)                    )?;
[1237](#1237)                }
[1238](#1238)                _ => {}
[1239](#1239)            }
[1240](#1240)        }
[1241](#1241)    }
[1242](#1242)
[1243](#1243)    lines.sort_unstable_by(|r1, r2| {
[1244](#1244)        if r1.call_depth < r2.call_depth {
[1245](#1245)            Ordering::Less
[1246](#1246)        } else if r1.call_depth > r2.call_depth {
[1247](#1247)            Ordering::Greater
[1248](#1248)        } else if r1.start_offset < r2.start_offset {
[1249](#1249)            Ordering::Less
[1250](#1250)        } else if r1.start_offset > r2.start_offset {
[1251](#1251)            Ordering::Greater
[1252](#1252)        } else {
[1253](#1253)            Ordering::Equal
[1254](#1254)        }
[1255](#1255)    });
[1256](#1256)
[1257](#1257)    Ok(lines)
[1258](#1258)}
[1259](#1259)
[1260](#1260)fn process_inlinee_symbols(
[1261](#1261)    symbols_iter: &mut SymbolIter,
[1262](#1262)    inlinees: &BTreeMap<IdIndex, Inlinee>,
[1263](#1263)    proc_offset: PdbInternalSectionOffset,
[1264](#1264)    site: InlineSiteSymbol,
[1265](#1265)    call_depth: u16,
[1266](#1266)    lines: &mut Vec<InlineRange>,
[1267](#1267)) -> Result<RangeSet2<u32>> {
[1268](#1268)    let mut ranges = RangeSet2::empty();
[1269](#1269)    let mut file_index = None;
[1270](#1270)    if let Some(inlinee) = inlinees.get(&site.inlinee) {
[1271](#1271)        let mut iter = inlinee.lines(proc_offset, &site);
[1272](#1272)        while let Ok(Some(line_info)) = iter.next() {
[1273](#1273)            let length = match line_info.length {
[1274](#1274)                Some(0) | None => {
[1275](#1275)                    continue;
[1276](#1276)                }
[1277](#1277)                Some(l) => l,
[1278](#1278)            };
[1279](#1279)            let start_offset = line_info.offset.offset;
[1280](#1280)            let end_offset = line_info.offset.offset + length;
[1281](#1281)            lines.push(InlineRange {
[1282](#1282)                start_offset,
[1283](#1283)                end_offset,
[1284](#1284)                call_depth,
[1285](#1285)                inlinee: site.inlinee,
[1286](#1286)                file_index: Some(line_info.file_index),
[1287](#1287)                line_start: Some(line_info.line_start),
[1288](#1288)            });
[1289](#1289)            ranges |= RangeSet::from(start_offset..end_offset);
[1290](#1290)            if file_index.is_none() {
[1291](#1291)                file_index = Some(line_info.file_index);
[1292](#1292)            }
[1293](#1293)        }
[1294](#1294)    }
[1295](#1295)
[1296](#1296)    let mut callee_ranges = RangeSet2::empty();
[1297](#1297)    while let Some(symbol) = symbols_iter.next()? {
[1298](#1298)        if symbol.index() >= site.end {
[1299](#1299)            break;
[1300](#1300)        }
[1301](#1301)        if let S_LPROC32 | S_LPROC32_ST | S_GPROC32 | S_GPROC32_ST | S_LPROC32_ID | S_GPROC32_ID
[1302](#1302)        | S_LPROC32_DPC | S_LPROC32_DPC_ID | S_INLINESITE | S_INLINESITE2 = symbol.raw_kind()
[1303](#1303)        {
[1304](#1304)            match symbol.parse() {
[1305](#1305)                Ok(SymbolData::Procedure(p)) => {
[1306](#1306)                    symbols_iter.skip_to(p.end)?;
[1308](#1308)                }
[1309](#1309)                Ok(SymbolData::InlineSite(site)) => {
[1310](#1310)                    callee_ranges |= process_inlinee_symbols(
[1311](#1311)                        symbols_iter,
[1312](#1312)                        inlinees,
[1313](#1313)                        proc_offset,
[1314](#1314)                        site,
[1315](#1315)                        call_depth + 1,
[1316](#1316)                        lines,
[1317](#1317)                    )?;
[1318](#1318)                }
[1319](#1319)                _ => {}
[1320](#1320)            }
[1321](#1321)        }
[1322](#1322)    }
[1323](#1323)
[1324](#1324)    if !ranges.is_superset(&callee_ranges) {
[1325](#1325)        let missing_ranges: RangeSet2<u32> = &callee_ranges - &ranges;
[1327](#1327)        for range in missing_ranges.iter() {
[1328](#1328)            let (start_offset, end_offset) = match range {
[1329](#1329)                RangeSetRange::Range(r) => (*r.start, *r.end),
[1330](#1330)                other => {
[1331](#1331)                    panic!("Unexpected range bounds {:?}", other);
[1332](#1332)                }
[1333](#1333)            };
[1334](#1334)            lines.push(InlineRange {
[1335](#1335)                start_offset,
[1336](#1336)                end_offset,
[1337](#1337)                call_depth,
[1338](#1338)                inlinee: site.inlinee,
[1339](#1339)                file_index,
[1340](#1340)                line_start: None,
[1341](#1341)            });
[1342](#1342)        }
[1343](#1343)        ranges |= missing_ranges;
[1344](#1344)    }
[1345](#1345)
[1346](#1346)    Ok(ranges)
[1347](#1347)}
[1348](#1348)

# Context in pdb_addr2line - Rust

`pub struct Context<'a, 's> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The main API of this crate. Resolves addresses to function information.

Create a [ Context](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html) manually. Most consumers will want to use

[instead.](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextPdbData.html#method.make_context)

`ContextPdbData::make_context`However, if you interact with a PDB directly and parse some of its contents for other uses, you may want to call this method in order to avoid overhead from repeatedly parsing the same streams.

#### pub fn [functions](https://docs.rs#method.functions)(&self) -> [FunctionIter](https://docs.rs/struct.FunctionIter.html)<'_, 'a, 's> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Iterate over all functions in the modules.

Find the function whose code contains the provided address. The return value only contains the function name and the rva range, but no file or line information.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/pdb_addr2line/lib.rs.html#475-665)

#### pub fn [find_frames](https://docs.rs#method.find_frames)(
    &self,
    probe: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[FunctionFrames](https://docs.rs/struct.FunctionFrames.html)<'_>>, [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)>

Find information about the source code which generated the instruction at the provided address. This information includes the function name, file name and line number, of the containing procedure and of any functions that were inlined into the procedure by the compiler, at that address.

A lot of information is cached so that repeated calls are fast.

# TypeFormatter in pdb_addr2line - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pdb-addr2line/0.12.0/pdb_addr2line/struct.TypeFormatter.html

`pub struct TypeFormatter<'a, 's> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Allows printing function signatures, for example for use in stack traces.

Procedure symbols in PDBs usually have a name string which only includes the function name,
and no function arguments. Instead, the arguments need to be obtained from the symbol’s type
information. [ TypeFormatter](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeFormatter.html) handles that.

The same is true for “inlinee” functions - these are referenced by their [ pdb::IdIndex](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/common/struct.IdIndex.html), and their

[’s name string again only contains the raw function name but no arguments and also no namespace or class name.](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/tpi/id/enum.IdData.html)

`IdData`[handles those, too, in](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeFormatter.html)

`TypeFormatter`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeFormatter.html#method.format_id)

`TypeFormatter::format_id`## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/pdb_addr2line/type_formatter.rs.html#114-257)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-TypeFormatter%3C'a,+'s%3E)### impl<'a, 's> [TypeFormatter](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeFormatter.html)<'a, 's>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/pdb_addr2line/type_formatter.rs.html#114-257)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-TypeFormatter%3C'a,+'s%3E)

### impl<'a, 's> [TypeFormatter](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeFormatter.html)<'a, 's>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/pdb_addr2line/type_formatter.rs.html#121-165)#### pub fn [new_from_parts](https://docs.rs#method.new_from_parts)(
    module_provider: &'a (dyn [ModuleProvider](https://docs.rs/trait.ModuleProvider.html)<'s> + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html)),
    modules: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Module](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/dbi/struct.Module.html)<'a>>,
    debug_info: &[DebugInformation](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/dbi/struct.DebugInformation.html)<'s>,

Return a string with the function or method signature, including return type (if
requested), namespace and/or class qualifiers, and arguments.
If the TypeIndex is 0, then only the raw name is emitted. In that case, the
name may need to go through additional demangling / “undecorating”, but this
is the responsibility of the caller.
This method is used for [ ProcedureSymbols](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/symbol/struct.ProcedureSymbol.html).
The module_index is the index of the module in which this procedure was found. It
is necessary in order to properly resolve cross-module references.

# ContextPdbData in pdb_addr2line - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pdb-addr2line/0.12.0/pdb_addr2line/struct.ContextPdbData.html

## Expand description

Allows to easily create a [ Context](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html) directly from a

[.](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/pdb/struct.PDB.html)

`pdb::PDB````
let pdb = pdb::PDB::open(stream)?;
let context_data = pdb_addr2line::ContextPdbData::try_from_pdb(pdb)?;
let context = context_data.make_context()?;
```
Implementation note:
It would be nice if a [ Context](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html) could be created from a

[directly, without going through an intermediate](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/pdb/struct.PDB.html)

`PDB`[object. However, there doesn’t seem to be an easy way to do this, due to certain lifetime dependencies: The](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextPdbData.html)

`ContextPdbData`[object wants to store certain objects inside itself (mostly for caching) which have a lifetime dependency on](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)

`Context`[, so the](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/modi/struct.ModuleInfo.html)

`pdb::ModuleInfo`[has to be owned outside of the](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/modi/struct.ModuleInfo.html)

`ModuleInfo`[. So the](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)

`Context`[object acts as that external](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextPdbData.html)

`ContextPdbData`[owner.](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/modi/struct.ModuleInfo.html)

`ModuleInfo`## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/pdb_addr2line/lib.rs.html#116-203)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-ContextPdbData%3C'p,+'s,+S%3E)### impl<'p, 's, S: [Source](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/source/trait.Source.html)<'s> + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + 's> [ContextPdbData](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextPdbData.html)<'p, 's, S>

Create a [ ContextPdbData](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextPdbData.html) from a

[. This parses many of the PDB streams and stores them in the](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/pdb/struct.PDB.html)

`PDB`[. This creator function takes an exclusive reference to the pdb object, for consumers that want to keep using the pdb object once the](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextPdbData.html)

`PartialOrd`[with those of another. The comparison works like short-circuit evaluation, returning a result without comparing the remaining elements. #### fn [sub_assign](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/arith/trait.SubAssign.html#tymethod.sub_assign)(&mut self, other: Self)

The intersection of a source flags value with the complement of a target flags value (`&!`).

This method is not equivalent to `self & !other` when `other` has unknown bits set.
`difference` won’t truncate `other`, but the `!` operator will.

If you use ContextPdbData you do not need to worry about this trait. This trait allows Context and TypeFormatter to request parsing of module info on-demand. It also does some lifetime acrobatics so that Context can cache objects which have a lifetime dependency on the module info.

# pdb_addr2line - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pdb-addr2line/latest/pdb_addr2line/

## Expand description

Resolve addresses to function names, and to file name and line number information, with the help of a PDB file. Inline stacks are supported.

The API of this crate is intended to be similar to the API of the
[ addr2line crate](https://docs.rs/addr2line/); the two

[APIs have comparable functionality. This crate is for PDB files whereas](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)

`Context``addr2line`
is for DWARF data (which is used in ELF and mach-o binaries, for example).This crate also has a [ TypeFormatter](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeFormatter.html) API which can be used to get function signature
strings independently from a

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)

`Context`To create a [ Context](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html), use

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextPdbData.html)

`ContextPdbData`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use pdb_addr2line::pdb; // (this is a re-export of the pdb crate)
fn look_up_addresses<'s, S: pdb::Source<'s> + Send + 's>(stream: S, addresses: &[u32]) -> std::result::Result<(), pdb_addr2line::Error> {
    let pdb = pdb::PDB::open(stream)?;
    let context_data = pdb_addr2line::ContextPdbData::try_from_pdb(pdb)?;
    let context = context_data.make_context()?;
    for address in addresses {
        if let Some(procedure_frames) = context.find_frames(*address)? {
            eprintln!("0x{:x} - {} frames:", address, procedure_frames.frames.len());
            for frame in procedure_frames.frames {
                let line_str = frame.line.map(|l| format!("{}", l));
                eprintln!(
                    "     {} at {}:{}",
                    frame.function.as_deref().unwrap_or("<unknown>"),
                    frame.file.as_deref().unwrap_or("??"),
                    line_str.as_deref().unwrap_or("??"),
                )
            }
        } else {
            eprintln!("{:x} - no frames found", address);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [maybe_owned](https://docs.rs/maybe-owned/0.3.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/maybe_owned/index.html);
- `pub use`- [pdb](https://docs.rs/pdb2/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/pdb2/index.html);

# bitflags 2.13.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bitflags/^2.0

# bitflags

`bitflags` generates flags enums with well-defined semantics and ergonomic end-user APIs.

You can use `bitflags` to:

- provide more user-friendly bindings to C APIs where flags may or may not be fully known in advance.
- generate efficient options types with string parsing and formatting support.

You can't use `bitflags` to:

-
guarantee only bits corresponding to defined flags will ever be set. `bitflags`allows access to the underlying bits type so arbitrary bits may be set.
-
define bitfields. `bitflags`only generates types where set bits denote the presence of some combination of flags.

## Usage

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "2.13.0"
```
and this to your source code:

```
use bitflags;
```
## Example

Generate a flags structure:

```
use bitflags;
// The `bitflags!` macro generates `struct`s that manage a set of flags.
bitflags!
```
## Cargo features

The `bitflags` library defines a few Cargo features that you can opt-in to:

- `std`: Implement the- `Error`trait on error types used by- `bitflags`.
- `serde`: Support deriving- `serde`traits on generated flags types.
- `arbitrary`: Support deriving- `arbitrary`traits on generated flags types.
- `bytemuck`: Support deriving- `bytemuck`traits on generated flags types.

Also see [ bitflags_derive](https://github.com/bitflags/bitflags-derive) for other flags-aware traits.

## Rust Version Support

The minimum supported Rust version is documented in the `Cargo.toml` file.
This may be bumped in minor releases as necessary.
